prompt.context: Royal Health Services is a regional healthcare system operating several hospitals and clinics in the Midwest. Due to market fragmentation and increased costs of providing care, their profit margin has continued to decrease.
prompt.question: The board of directors has asked you to develop a strategy to increase profitability over the next two years.

clarifying_info.q: How many hospitals and clinics does Royal Health operate, and where?
clarifying_info.a: Royal Health operates 7 hospitals and 40+ clinics in Missouri, Kansas, and Nebraska. Clinics are less of a focus of this case.

clarifying_info.q: What patient populations does Royal Health serve?
clarifying_info.a: Royal Health provides all levels of care to all ages.

clarifying_info.q: Can Royal Health attract patients from outside the region?
clarifying_info.a: Royal Health is not nationally known for the care provided and is therefore unlikely to attract patients from outside the region.

clarifying_info.q: What is happening in the broader healthcare industry?
clarifying_info.a: The healthcare industry has had considerable consolidation in recent years. Regulatory changes and pressure from payers have made it increasingly difficult for individual hospitals and smaller health systems to maintain profitability.

exhibits.title: Regional Health System Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table comparing Royal Health Services against three other regional health systems across 2016 revenue, 2016 operating income, number of hospitals, states of operation, and number of employees.

Health System #2.states: CO, KS, IL, IN, KY, OH, PA, TX, WA

exhibits.title: 2016 Corporate Shared Services – % of Total Operating Expense
exhibits.shows: A table listing five corporate shared service categories (Finance, HR, IT, Legal, Revenue Cycle) with each category's percentage of total operating expense for Health System #3 and Royal Health Services separately, plus the combined total operating expense of the two organizations.

framework: Revenue levers: pricing (highly regulated, limited room), volume (constrained by regional footprint)
Cost levers: labor, SG&A, IT, supplier contracts, physician group contracts, facilities
Competitive landscape: assess market fragmentation and peer performance
M&A / scale: evaluate merger or acquisition targets to achieve scale and improve margins

questions.prompt: After presenting your framework, where would you like to start and why?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate recognizes that pricing is highly regulated and that Royal Health cannot easily attract out-of-region patients, so revenue upside is limited. The candidate should pivot toward cost reduction and then competitive/M&A strategy. An excellent candidate immediately flags that a fragmented market is a signal to consider M&A.

questions.prompt: What internal cost reduction opportunities should Royal Health explore?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm: reduction in labor expense, SG&A, IT costs; renegotiating contracts with medical suppliers and physician groups; overall costs of patient care; facilities cost reduction. After brainstorming, the interviewer should note that these are not areas that will drive significant impact at this time and guide the candidate toward competition and/or M&A.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 1. What are your initial thoughts?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate operating margins for all four organizations and note that Royal Health is the worst performer. Candidate should observe that Health System 2's scale likely drives its higher margin. Candidate should identify geographic overlap: Health System 1 overlaps (KS, MO); Health System 2 has no overlap; Health System 3 shares only MO. Candidate should then consider these as M&A targets rather than competitors. Excellent candidate calculates combined revenue of $4.2B (Royal + HS3) and notes scale benefits.

steps: Royal is the worst performer; HS2 demonstrates that scale drives margin improvement
Combined operating income (no savings): $72M + $90M = $162M; margin = $162M / $4,200M = 3.86% (approx 4.76% using combined op expense base)
math.answer: Royal Health margin = 3% (lowest); HS2 at 8% shows scale benefit; HS3 is the preferred merger target for scale + new markets

questions.prompt: After agreeing that a merger with Health System #3 is the best option, what are some of the ways to create value through a merger?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm multiple categories: Synergies (reduce corporate shared service costs via centralization/headcount reduction; reduce redundant investments; centralize overlapping medical services in MO); Scale (new market access in IL/OK; greater bargaining power with suppliers and payers; diversified revenue base); Growth (integrated care model; standardized clinical processes; improved patient experience and reputation). Strong candidates organize their brainstorm into clearly labeled buckets.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 2. Calculate the potential savings from consolidating corporate shared services after a merger with Health System #3.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that the combined shared services currently total 35% of operating expense. By taking the lowest percentage from each category, the combined entity can reduce shared services to 28%. Candidate should apply this to the combined operating expense of ~$4,000M. An excellent candidate also layers in Exhibit 1 data to compute the new combined operating margin.

math.setup: Combined total operating expense = $4,038M (round to ~$4,000M). Current shared services = 35% of op expense. Optimized shared services = lowest % per category. Finance: min(6%,3%)=3%; HR: min(4%,7%)=4%; IT: min(8%,11%)=8%; Legal: min(4%,5%)=4%; Revenue Cycle: min(13%,9%)=9%; Optimized total = 3+4+8+4+9 = 28%.
steps: (Bonus) Combined operating income with savings: $4,200M – $3,720M = $480M (approx $442M per casebook)
math.answer: Savings of ~$280M; new total operating expense ~$3,720M; combined margin improves significantly from 3% to approximately 10–13%

brainstorming.prompt: What are some of the ways to create value through a merger between Royal Health Services and Health System #3?

categories.name: Synergies
ideas: Reduction of corporate shared service costs (admin, finance, legal, IT, revenue cycle) through centralization
Potential headcount reduction in duplicated functions
Reduce level of initial and future capital investments needed
Centralize medical services in overlapping MO market to improve patient experience and reduce cost

categories.name: Scale
ideas: Opportunity to grow and diversify business by accessing new markets (IL, OK)
Greater market share leading to increased bargaining power with suppliers and health plans

categories.name: Growth & Quality
ideas: Integrated care model across the combined organization
Standardize clinical processes to improve outcomes and efficiency
Better reputation in the industry attracting more patients
Improved patient experience through coordinated care

recommendation: Royal Health Services should proceed with exploring the merger with Health System #3
The merger offers significant shared services savings of approximately $280M, reducing combined operating expense from ~$4,000M to ~$3,720M
The combined entity gains scale, enters new markets (IL, OK), and increases bargaining power, positioning it to improve its operating margin well above the current 3%
risks: Anti-trust and regulatory scrutiny given healthcare consolidation environment
Synergies may not be fully realized due to integration challenges or cultural differences
Changes to the regulatory climate (e.g., ACA reimbursement changes) could affect the business case
Integration complexity across 13 hospitals and ~49,000 employees in multiple states
next_steps: Announce that a merger agreement is being pursued; sign a definitive agreement and seek regulatory approval
Complete comprehensive due diligence on Health System #3 financials, operations, and liabilities
Plan integration roadmap including shared services consolidation timeline
Consider any necessary rebranding of the combined entity
